audit.title: Cross-Chain Token Standard (EVM)

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Opens with a scope statement — "This section provides detailed guidance for integrating tokens with Chainlink CCIP on EVM-compatible blockchains" — but the implied question ("what is the CCT standard?") is never answered. A lifted chunk describes the *section*, not the *concept*.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Clean bullet list with bolded, linked labels and one-line descriptions; measured facts confirm 0 level skips and one coherent section. Weak only because there is no H2 hierarchy — it is a single 87-word block by design.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Facts show 3 numerals, 0 with units, 0 hex identifiers, no version strings. Almost entirely qualitative. No supported-chain list, no counts, no limits.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 6 internal links, 0 external. Appropriate for a hub, but no link to the CCIP spec or a canonical concept definition raises no external credibility.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: No one-to-two-sentence definition of "Cross-Chain Token Standard" or "CCT" near first use — the single most impactful gap for a concept page.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Visible `Last Updated` date and clean semantic heading are positives; but facts confirm 0 JSON-LD blocks, missing canonical, absent `datePublished`/`dateModified`, no `og`/`twitter` tags. No `TechArticle` schema.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No code present. Acceptable for a hub page, but nothing here aids agent execution.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Serves "where do I find X" navigation only. No "what is…", "how do I…", or troubleshooting phrasing.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; prose is unambiguous and consistently names "Chainlink CCIP" and "CCTs." No action needed.

audit.summary: This is a thin **section-index / hub page** (92 words, one H1, five links to child pages) whose job is to route readers to Architecture, Tokens, Token Pools, Registration, and Upgradability subpages. Its strength is clean, fluent routing prose with a visible `Last Updated: 2025-05-19`. Its biggest opportunity is that it never defines what the "Cross-Chain Token Standard (CCT)" actually *is* — so it offers a generative engine nothing quotable and little reason to be cited over the deeper child pages. Verdict: adequate as navigation, but currently a low-value retrieval target that should carry a canonical definition and schema to earn citations.

recommendations.title: Add a canonical definition of the Cross-Chain Token Standard
recommendations.where: First paragraph, before the link list.
recommendations.issue: "This section provides detailed guidance for integrating tokens…" — describes the section, not the concept.
recommendations.change: Add a self-contained lead sentence, e.g. "The Chainlink CCIP Cross-Chain Token (CCT) standard is a token-development framework that lets token issuers deploy and manage their own token pools to enable secure cross-chain transfers via CCIP, without permissionless liquidity pools or Chainlink involvement in deployment." Then keep the link list.
recommendations.why: Gives engines a verbatim-liftable definition; defends against parametric priors that would otherwise answer "what is CCT" generically or wrongly.

recommendations.title: Add concrete specifics to the lead
recommendations.issue: Facts show 0 numerals with units, no supported-chain or version detail.
recommendations.change: State a quantifiable fact, e.g. the number/names of supported EVM chains, the two token-pool models (burn-and-mint, lock-and-release), or the required contract interfaces. Even one accurate figure raises retrieval lift.
recommendations.why: Quantitative claims are among the highest-lift changes for generative visibility.

recommendations.title: Add `TechArticle` JSON-LD and canonical URL
recommendations.issue: Facts confirm 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, `dateModified` absent from structured data.
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` schema with `headline`, `dateModified: 2025-05-19`, `inLanguage`, and a self-referential `canonical`. Mirror the visible "Last Updated" into `dateModified`.
recommendations.why: Structured freshness and canonical signals improve agent parsing and E-E-A-T trust.

recommendations.title: Phrase the child-link descriptions as the questions users ask
recommendations.issue: Labels are noun-phrases ("Token Pools", "Upgradability") that miss symptom/how-to queries.
recommendations.change: Append or reframe with intent phrasing, e.g. "Token Pools — how to choose between burn-and-mint and lock-and-release pools"; "Upgradability — how to upgrade a token pool contract."
recommendations.why: Headings phrased as user questions win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses.

recommendations.title: Add one external/primary reference
recommendations.issue: 0 external links; no link to the CCIP canonical concept or spec.
recommendations.change: Inline-link "CCIP" to the top-level CCIP concept page or architecture spec.
recommendations.why: Attributable claims raise credibility and citation rate.

antiPatterns: **Thin content as a standalone retrieval target** — 92 words with no definition; the page functions only as navigation and offers little liftable substance. Not fluff or stuffing, but low citation value.
No stale-date issue (dated 2025-05-19, visible), no ambiguous pronouns, no keyword stuffing.
offPageNotes: Head metadata could not be verified — the CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a full schema/canonical read; JSON-LD and OG tags are site-template concerns.
The page already references `/llms.txt` — good site-level discoverability signal; ensure this hub and its children are listed there.
Whether this hub is *outranked* by its own child pages in generative answers is best confirmed with a probe run; no probe data was provided here.
